# Saved matched-control outcome groups

TokenJunkieLabs scientific engineering. This feature compares explicitly selected, already completed native control designs. It does not prepare or execute a native model, change a design, select an automatic winner, or turn deterministic placements into independent statistical replicates.

The complete current owner instructions are retained in source/MULTIVARIATE_CONTROL_OWNER_DIRECTION.md together with CURRENT_OWNER_DIRECTION.md v2026-10-13.4. The original equipped receiving course must use and LOOK at the actual final application and every outgoing attachment; source inspection is not rendered acceptance. Keep current source owners, native run identities and existing application/session custody.

## What the analyst chooses

Select the exact saved control designs in the intended display order, the actually produced annual quantities, one quantity scope, a title and a scientific question. All designs must be accepted and adopted through the original matched-control engine. They must bind the same original project, grid, parameter profile, baseline and restoration. Each corresponding control, baseline and restoration must be complete.

The chosen designs may differ in explicit strata, optional aligned slope/connectivity sources, exclusion masks, calipers or other retained design choices. Their full source classifications, physical definitions, bin rules, pair rosters, exclusions and residual balances remain attached. A different title or saved ID does not establish a different spatial placement.

The catalogue distinguishes ready and unfinished adopted controls. Preview verifies the actual current original selections, producing-model versions, artifact units, full file hashes, executed categorical inputs and retained design/adoption bindings. It never silently removes a control or quantity. An unavailable or incompatible member must be resolved explicitly before preparing that exact group.

Selection shape (replace the illustrative IDs with actual retained values):

~~~json
{
  "schema": "upstate.multivariate-control-outcome-selection/v1",
  "title": "Author's explicit placement comparison",
  "reason": "Author's scientific question and selection rationale",
  "design_ids": ["ACTUAL_FIRST_DESIGN_ID", "ACTUAL_SECOND_DESIGN_ID"],
  "pollutants": ["nitrogen_export", "phosphorus_export", "sediment_export"],
  "quantity_scope": "reporting"
}
~~~

No example supplies scientific bin edges, invented native quantities, causal conclusions or default placement rankings.

## Support and signs

The primary report compares every chosen control on **group-common support**. For each pollutant separately this is the exact selected region intersected with finite native values in the baseline, restoration and every explicitly selected control. Its window-addressed mask SHA, complete native run roster, common count/area and every individual valid count are retained.

Separate **per-design** rows use that design's finite baseline/restoration/control intersection. These retain coverage diagnostics and complete unranked totals. Different per-design masks cannot support a direct ranking or subtraction of totals. The report shows the support lost when moving from each triple to the group-common intersection.

| Quantity | Direct calculation on the declared support | Meaning of a positive result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline minus restoration | B − R | Lower modeled export under the retained restoration |
| Baseline minus control | B − C | Lower modeled export under that selected control |
| Control minus restoration | C − R | Lower modeled export under restoration than that control |

Native finite support is not reduced by missing categorical support. Categorical change/unchanged/unknown partitions remain separately visible. An empty common native mask yields unavailable values and a concrete reason, never zero or a silently dropped design.

The implementation reads original native values as Float64 through the original receiving_waters reader. It accumulates direct cell differences with the original compensated siting accumulator. It does not subtract rounded displayed aggregates or reuse pairwise Float32 difference rasters for a new scientific calculation. Group rows must share the same mask, baseline/restoration mass and B−R; group support cannot exceed its corresponding triple.

## Reporting and model-domain scopes

These are separate saved selections and scientific identities.

* **reporting** uses the original retained reporting mask and original mass-per-pixel artifacts. They are read once without multiplying by pixel area again.
* **model_domain** uses the exact original prepared model_domain geometry, including its admitted buffer, and retained native output rasters. The grid bounding rectangle or valid NLCD pixels are not a substitute for the model polygon.

Full-domain conversion is admitted only with actual observed producing InVEST 3.20.0, original native_units matching the retained per-hectare quantity and the exact native grid pixel_area_ha. Original native density is multiplied by those hectares once. A matching requested-version string is insufficient. This explicit boundary avoids applying current density conventions to historical native releases with other units.

Annual nitrogen/phosphorus quantities are kg/year; annual sediment is metric tonnes/year. GeoTIFF differences retain kg/pixel/year or metric_tonnes/pixel/year. These represent modeled stream export attributed to source pixels inside the declared support. They are not concentration, pollutant delivery to an intake, observed benefits or an isolated causal effect. Flow routing and retention can change outcomes on unchanged source cells.

The frozen report links the official guide for each actual retained producing model/version. Original source records and conversions remain authoritative; full-domain admission is deliberately limited as above.

## Area and spatial identity

Whole-scenario changed area, changed area inside the selected region, and changed area on common native support are distinct denominators. All three remain in the complete result/CSV, with explicitly named normalized rates and unavailable reasons. Equal area/class budgets do not prove equal physical connectivity or causal attribution.

Every executed restoration/control categorical band is compared by exact values and validity to its retained original footprint. Whole changed-cell counts, hectares and baseline-origin class budgets must match the accepted design. The unchanged baseline is checked against the actual prepared categorical grid.

A deterministic placement SHA covers the addressed changed mask and original/destination classes. Identical final placements are explicitly marked even if their saved titles/design IDs differ. Pairwise changed-cell intersection, union and Jaccard are retained. These measures describe spatial overlap; distinct placements are not asserted to be independent random replicates. The report supplies descriptive individual outcomes without confidence intervals, standard errors or a fabricated replicate count.

## Original native API and CLI

The native facade is model.multivariate_control_outcomes:

* catalog(workspace) lists adopted designs, readiness, available quantities, saved groups and concrete issues.
* preview(workspace, selection) returns the normalized selection, exact input binding and proposed identity. State is ready or existing.
* prepare(workspace, selection, progress=None) produces or reopens the exact immutable group. Its progress callback receives one dictionary.
* inspect(workspace, outcome_id) verifies the original stored identity, complete assessment, exact native bindings, source CAS and every retained file.
* files(workspace, outcome_id) returns the original workspace-relative download descriptors.

There is no outcome execute command. Native controls are completed separately through the original accepted experiment lifecycle.

From the actual application root and original environment:

~~~sh
python -m model.multivariate_control_outcomes_cli catalog --workspace ACTUAL_WORKSPACE
python -m model.multivariate_control_outcomes_cli preview --workspace ACTUAL_WORKSPACE --selection AUTHORED_GROUP.json
python -m model.multivariate_control_outcomes_cli prepare --workspace ACTUAL_WORKSPACE --selection AUTHORED_GROUP.json
python -m model.multivariate_control_outcomes_cli inspect --workspace ACTUAL_WORKSPACE --id ACTUAL_OUTCOME_ID
python -m model.multivariate_control_outcomes_cli files --workspace ACTUAL_WORKSPACE --id ACTUAL_OUTCOME_ID
~~~

Native progress is written to multivariate-control-outcomes/ID/progress.json and emitted to stderr by the CLI. The final JSON has state complete. Invalid/incomplete scientific inputs produce their original concrete exception before a completed record is issued. A missing inspect target raises FileNotFoundError. The immutable identity binds the normalized scientific choices, original design/adoption/run/footprint/artifact descriptors, observed execution provenance and the exact producer/renderer source.

If report/source import acknowledgement is lost, the next identical prepare verifies and reuses the already-frozen report recipe and complete report/PDF/map bytes. It does not rerender a previously issued PDF under the same identity. Repeating an existing complete selection verifies and reopens it.

## Reports, maps and complete source

The result directory contains:

| Member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| outcome.json | Complete native record and original source choice |
| assessment.json | Complete frozen numerical result, selection, binding and semantic identities |
| selection.json / input-binding.json / identity.json | Authored choices and exact original input/producer binding |
| outcomes.csv | Both support modes, direct masses/differences, all denominators, rates and unavailable reasons |
| partitions.csv | Every changed/unchanged/unknown categorical source partition |
| placements.csv / placement-overlaps.csv | All authored design metadata, exact mask identities and overlap measures |
| report.html / report.pdf / report.md / report-data.json | Complete readable original scientific report in the maintained renderer |
| maps/design-N/SUPPORT/QUANTITY-DIFFERENCE.tif | Full original-grid Float64 signed map for all three differences and both support modes |
| maps/...-support.tif | Exact finite support mask; outside support is NoData, not zero |
| maps/...preview.json / SVG | Bounded display values, source descriptor, CRS/bounds and readable common-legend map |
| scientific-figures.json / outcome-*.svg | Original native figure specifications and complete plotted values |
| originals/DESIGN_ID/design.json / adoption.json | Exact accepted scientific design and original native adoption records |
| implementation/ | Complete source bodies used to produce the assessment, report and figures |
| report-source.json / sources.json | Ordinary OBSERVED_CONTEXT document and full original companion inventory |

The directly viewable map previews use nearest-neighbour display sampling only and preserve the original geographic aspect ratio. They may omit small features. Full-resolution GeoTIFFs are the scientific maps. Grayscale previews use the same full-raster absolute range for a pollutant across selected controls: light positive C−R means lower export under restoration; dark negative means higher; middle gray is zero. Distinct diagonal hatching denotes NoData. The shared numeric legend preserves the actual sign and magnitude. Every map retains its quantity, support definition, design, native run roster and units.

The PDF/HTML uses the original scientific_report and scientific_figures renderers. Its primary tables use group-common results, explicit signs/units, all three area denominators, and complete design rules/residual balance. Long rosters are continued across report sections without dropping rows. Scientific-source recipes use the maintained observed-context figure specification/companion contract; no generic source validator is relaxed.

The new source is an ordinary kind=document, role=OBSERVED_CONTEXT entry. Its exact body and every companion are preserved through original source CAS. Select it in the original Sources composer to build an ordered scientific edition. Source/report selection does not rerun native models or infer a new saved edition.

## Editable selected Study and independent receiving

The typed root is **multivariate-control-outcomes**. Use the original Study selector to select the exact saved group. It retains the entire outcome directory and every selected original editable control design. Existing design visitors retain source collections, exact grid/profile, original B/R runs, compiled footprint completion tree and the adopted C scenario/run/footprint/experiment, including current legitimate native progress.

The shared Study engine dynamically consumes the existing control helper's root/document/lock/label exports. This feature adds an owned outcome adapter to that helper; it does not replace the original generic closure or portable writer. Outcome and design writers retain their existing operation locks, and original source/file identities are verified by the same frozen export process.

A selected scientific edition containing this exact same-project outcome source follows the same typed outcome root. Equivalent reimports under a different collection selector are accepted only with the complete identical original native body/companions. Foreign report sources remain contained CAS documents; they never borrow local project IDs. Existing archives without this new outcome root/source retain their original receiving semantics.

Export through the existing Study workflow; restore through the original portable/Study receiving workflow into an independent destination. On the recipient open the actual saved outcome, each original design and native experiment, all report/data/GIS members, and the original source choice. No design is reconstructed from prose and no model is executed to verify receiving. Full Workspace export remains available as the broader original workflow.

## One original equipped receiving course

Extend the already accepted matched-control native/browser course on its actual complete restored workspace. Preserve the original regional/teaching and later completed cases, current native handles, source writer and application identity. A555's actual completed teaching workspace is supported by the original matched-control receipt; do not fabricate a Geographic preparation ID to enter a browser chapter.

Use an explicitly authored group of actually adopted complete controls. Preview it, prepare the report-only comparison, record actual outcome/source IDs, open/reopen the saved desk, download and inspect complete reports/maps/CSV/JSON, and export/restore its selected Study. The primary table and same-pollutant support hashes must match the native frozen result.

The producing receiver must personally open/run/render the exact outgoing application and LOOK at it at desktop/screenshare and narrow390px. Operate important controls, saved reopening, authored selection edits, populated/empty/loading/error states and every download. Open/view every attachment: HTML/PDF, tables/spreadsheets, JSON, maps/SVG/TIFF and archive contents, including the restored working project. Capturing screenshots without viewing them is insufficient. Fix unreadable, clipped, overflowed, cramped, broken or unstyled output in this original course.

Source review, API inspection and V8 checks are not native/GDAL or visual acceptance. This authoring seat does not claim execution it has not performed. The equipped owner reports the actual completed course or its first concrete exception.

## Ownership and attribution

Current owner direction v2026-10-13.4 and the complete standing rendered-product instruction remain in the consumed source family. Work continues under the original expanded post-call orders; preserve native work rather than repeating cases. Keep TokenJunkieLabs attribution on the application, source/report and attachments. Scientific interpretation and the client relationship remain with the prime and scientist.

This implementation authorizes no provider purchase, payment, contract signature, private repository, hosted Actions or extra fleet session. No external customer/prospect messages are sent by the outcome engine. Existing actual source rights, scientific choices and native execution owners remain authoritative.

# Native matched-control outcome desk

TokenJunkieLabs • Original Upper Savannah application • 13 October 2026

## Analyst course

Open **Matched controls → Native control outcomes**. Select completed, adopted designs in the intended display order. Every selected design must share its original baseline, restoration, native grid and parameter profile. Choose nitrogen, phosphorus or sediment outputs actually present in all selected runs, choose the original reporting area or the complete retained model domain, and state the scientific comparison question.

**Review native sources** binds the exact completed run outputs, observed producing model versions, original quantity conversion, domain geometry, adopted designs and original source descriptors. **Prepare outcome comparison** submits `control.outcomes.prepare` to the original persistent task queue. Preparation reads retained native outputs; it does not execute InVEST. A changed binding requires a fresh preview.

The initial result uses **all selected controls on identical cells**. The primary rows are the annual B, R and C masses plus direct B−R, B−C and C−R differences on one common finite mask per pollutant. Positive C−R means less modeled annual stream delivery under restoration. Signed zero and negative outcomes remain visible. Every selected control appears in original selection order.

**Each baseline / restoration / control triple** preserves individual support. Its masks may differ between controls; read those rows as separate native coverage and scenario results. The common all-control roster, individual run valid-cell counts and exact support hashes remain available beside the values.

## Interpretation and original quantities

Annual nitrogen/phosphorus values retain the original kg/year units; sediment retains its native annual mass unit. Values are source-cell exports delivered to modeled streams. Region totals do not give intake load, concentration or observed improvement.

Changed-area tables retain whole-scenario, region and common-native changed hectares as distinct denominators. Each displayed rate retains its own label; a zero denominator stays unavailable. Converted, unchanged and unknown categorical source-cell partitions describe where modeled changes originate. Routing and retention can change output at unchanged source cells.

Placement hashes identify the actual original changed cells. Repeated placements remain marked; they do not create independent replications. Original strata, selected optional covariate definitions, source provenance and residual balance stay attached.

## Persistent work and original Study

Choices are retained under `upstate-multivariate-control-outcome-desk-v1:<workspace>`. The complete immutable request is saved and read back before dispatch. If a response is lost, **Recover same request** reuses the original operation identity. A late response is written to its original project's saved desk even if the analyst has navigated elsewhere.

Export/reopen retains choices and original task receipts. The original Study selector lists **Matched-control native outcomes** under `multivariate-control-outcomes`; its Open action navigates to this original desk and inspects the retained result. Complete Workspace/Study closure follows the original producer's typed lineage, including source reports and full map files.

## Original interfaces

- Registered view and extension: `multivariate-control-outcomes`.
- Factory: `createMultivariateControlOutcomesWorkbench`.
- Public reopening: `openSavedOutcome({workspace_key,outcome_id,isCurrent})`.
- POST reads: `/api/multivariate-control-outcomes/catalog`, `preview`, `inspect`, `progress`.
- Queue action: `control.outcomes.prepare`, payload `{selection,expected_id}`.
- Inspect payload: `{outcome_id}`; progress payload: `{task_id}`.
- Native model ports: `catalog/preview/prepare/inspect/files`; progress callback receives one dictionary.

Result files are verified against original Workspace-relative descriptors before issuing original download tickets. Reports, source figures, CSV tables, full-resolution Float64 differences and support maps use those tickets.

## Existing native receiving

Continue the original `integration/multivariate_control_native_receiving.py` and existing geographic browser runner's accepted matched-control chapter. Native receiving authors actual selections from its completed original project. Exercise populated results, same-mask comparisons, original task recovery, report/map downloads and reopened Study. Open and LOOK at actual relevant desktop/narrow/loading/empty/error states and outgoing attachments under current owner directions. Browser receiving fixes product defects directly; the maintained application and completed native output remain the deliverable.

def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def checked_hash(value, label):
    if not isinstance(value, str) or HASH.fullmatch(value) is None:
        raise ValueError(label + ": expected a lowercase SHA-256")
    return value


def checked_name(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str) or value not in ALLOWED:
        raise ValueError("Unexpected Decision studies source path: " + repr(value))
    return value


def records(document, label):
    if not isinstance(document, dict):
        raise ValueError(label + ": expected a source packet object")
    files = document.get("files")
    if isinstance(files, list):
        result = files
    elif isinstance(files, dict):
        metadata = document.get("file_metadata", {})
        if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
            raise ValueError(label + ": malformed file_metadata")
        result = []
        for name, item in files.items():
            if isinstance(item, str):
                meta = metadata.get(name, {})
                if not isinstance(meta, dict):
                    raise ValueError(label + ": malformed metadata for " + name)
                result.append(dict(meta, path=name, content=item))
            elif isinstance(item, dict):
                if "path" in item and item["path"] != name:
                    raise ValueError(label + ": conflicting path for " + name)
                result.append(dict(item, path=name))
            else:
                raise ValueError(label + ": malformed file record")
    else:
        raise ValueError(label + ": missing files")
    if not result:
        raise ValueError(label + ": empty source packet")
    return result



def transport_document(text):
    # Canvas may insert NBSP indentation. Preserve quoted source strings here;
    # repair any affected source body only under its declared hash below.
    normalized, quoted, escaped = [], False, False
    for char in text:
        if quoted:
            normalized.append(char)
            if escaped:
                escaped = False
            elif char == "\\":
                escaped = True
            elif char == '"':
                quoted = False
        else:
            normalized.append(" " if char == "\u00a0" else char)
            if char == '"':
                quoted = True
    return json.loads("".join(normalized))


def read_layers(paths):
    final, allowed, origins = {}, {}, {}
    for path in paths:
        packet_path = Path(path).resolve(strict=True)
        document = transport_document(packet_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
        seen = set()
        for item in records(document, str(packet_path)):
            if not isinstance(item, dict):
                raise ValueError(str(packet_path) + ": malformed file record")
            name = checked_name(item.get("path"))
            if name in seen:
                raise ValueError(str(packet_path) + ": duplicate file " + name)
            seen.add(name)
            expected = checked_hash(item.get("sha256"), name)
            size = item.get("bytes")
            if type(size) is not int or size < 0:
                raise ValueError(name + ": expected an exact nonnegative byte length")
            if "content_base64" in item:
                if "content" in item or not isinstance(item["content_base64"], str):
                    raise ValueError(name + ": select one full source encoding")
                data = base64.b64decode(item["content_base64"], validate=True)
                content = data.decode("utf-8")
            else:
                content = item.get("content")
                if not isinstance(content, str):
                    raise ValueError(name + ": full UTF-8 content is required")
                data = content.encode("utf-8")
                if len(data) != size or sha(data) != expected:
                    candidate = content.replace("\u00a0", " ").encode("utf-8")
                    if len(candidate) == size and sha(candidate) == expected:
                        data, content = candidate, candidate.decode("utf-8")
            if len(data) != size or sha(data) != expected:
                raise ValueError(name + ": incoming byte length or SHA-256 differs")
            if name.endswith(".py"):
                ast.parse(content, filename=name)
            elif name.endswith(".json"):
                json.loads(content)
            previous = allowed.setdefault(name, set())
            if name in final:
                previous.add(sha(final[name]))
            for key in PREIMAGE_KEYS:
                value = item.get(key)
                if value is not None:
                    values = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
                    if not values:
                        raise ValueError(name + " " + key + ": expected at least one preimage SHA-256")
                    for expected_before in values:
                        previous.add(checked_hash(expected_before, name + " " + key))
            final[name], origins[name] = data, str(packet_path)
    return final, allowed, origins


def target_path(application, name):
    # Reject symlink components, including links that currently point inside
    # the application: an authored source leaf must have one stable location.
    current = application
    for component in PurePosixPath(name).parts:
        current = current / component
        if current.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError("Preserve and reconcile source symlink: " + name)
    if current.exists() and not current.is_file():
        raise ValueError("Expected regular source file: " + name)
    return current


def read_existing(application, name):
    path = target_path(application, name)
    return path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else None


def assembled_data(application, pending, name):
    if name in pending:
        return pending[name]
    data = read_existing(application, name)
    if data is None:
        raise ValueError("Receive the complete application/component first; missing " + name)
    return data

def prepare_legacy_retirement(application, pending):
    old = read_existing(application, LEGACY)
    backup = read_existing(application, RETIRED)
    if old is not None and (len(old), sha(old)) not in LEGACY_PREDECESSORS:
        raise ValueError("Preserve and compose the newer legacy decision registration: " + LEGACY)
    if backup is not None and (len(backup), sha(backup)) not in LEGACY_PREDECESSORS:
        raise ValueError("Preserve the existing decision-registration retirement record: " + RETIRED)
    if old is not None and backup is not None and old != backup:
        raise ValueError("Preserve both distinct original decision registrations before retirement")
    descriptor = json.loads(assembled_data(application, pending, "operator/extensions/robust-workbench.json"))
    ours = set(descriptor.get("backend", {}).get("actions", []))
    directory = target_path(application, "operator/extensions/robust-workbench.json").parent
    for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.json")):
        relative = path.relative_to(application).as_posix()
        if relative in (LEGACY, "operator/extensions/robust-workbench.json"):
            continue
        content = read_existing(application, relative)
        registration = json.loads(content)
        shared = ours & set(registration.get("backend", {}).get("actions", []))
        if shared:
            raise ValueError("Compose the existing action owner before installation: " +
                             relative + " (" + ", ".join(sorted(shared)) + ")")
    return old, backup


def run(application, packet_paths, *, dry_run=False):
    application = Path(application).resolve(strict=True)
    if not application.is_dir():
        raise ValueError("Application must be a directory")
    pending, allowed, origins = read_layers(packet_paths)
    lock_root = application / ".locks"
    if lock_root.is_symlink():
        raise ValueError("Preserve and reconcile the application's .locks symlink")
    lock_root.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    lock_path = lock_root / "extension-install.lock"
    if lock_path.is_symlink():
        raise ValueError("Preserve and reconcile the extension installer lock symlink")
    with lock_path.open("a+") as lock:
        # Share the original extension installer's lock; do not create a
        # competing independent lock for modifications to the same application.
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        originals, modes, conflicts = {}, {}, []
        for name, data in pending.items():
            path = target_path(application, name)
            before = path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else None
            originals[name] = before
            modes[name] = stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode) if before is not None else 0o644
            if before is not None and before != data and sha(before) not in allowed[name]:
                conflicts.append({"path": name, "actual_sha256": sha(before),
                                  "incoming_sha256": sha(data),
                                  "allowed_preimages": sorted(allowed[name])})
        if conflicts:
            raise ValueError("Newer or unrecognized authored files preserved; compose these exact sources first:\n" +
                             json.dumps(conflicts, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
        verify_composition(application, pending)
        legacy, retired = prepare_legacy_retirement(application, pending)
        # Publish the new registration only after its provider and assets exist.
        changed = sorted((name for name in pending if originals[name] != pending[name]),
                         key=lambda name: (name == "operator/extensions/robust-workbench.json", name))
        receipt = {
            "schema": "upstate.robust-workbench-install/v1",
            "application": str(application), "dry_run": dry_run,
            "changed": changed,
            "retired_registration": {"path": LEGACY, "retained_as": RETIRED,
                                     "sha256": sha(legacy)} if legacy is not None else None,
            "files": [{"path": name, "bytes": len(data), "sha256": sha(data),
                       "previous_sha256": sha(originals[name]) if originals[name] is not None else None,
                       "packet": origins[name]} for name, data in sorted(pending.items())],
        }
        if dry_run or (not changed and legacy is None):
            return receipt
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".robust-install-", dir=application) as temporary:
            staging = Path(temporary)
            for name in changed:
                staged = staging / name
                staged.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                with staged.open("wb") as stream:
                    stream.write(pending[name])
                    stream.flush()
                    os.fsync(stream.fileno())
                staged.chmod(modes[name])
            # Reconcile all inputs once more before the first replacement.
            for name in pending:
                if read_existing(application, name) != originals[name]:
                    raise RuntimeError("Concurrent authored change preserved at " + name)
            if (read_existing(application, LEGACY) != legacy or
                    read_existing(application, RETIRED) != retired):
                raise RuntimeError("Concurrent legacy registration changes preserved")
            if legacy is not None:
                # The known old descriptor owns the same twelve actions. Retain
                # its exact bytes outside *.json so the registry has one owner.
                os.replace(target_path(application, LEGACY), target_path(application, RETIRED))
            for name in changed:
                target = target_path(application, name)
                if read_existing(application, name) != originals[name]:
                    raise RuntimeError("Concurrent authored change preserved at " + name +
                                       "; compose current source and rerun the same packets")
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                os.replace(staging / name, target)
        # An interrupted install is restartable because incoming-identical
        # files are accepted and all remaining replacements retain preimages.
        for name, data in pending.items():
            if read_existing(application, name) != data:
                raise RuntimeError("Installed source changed during readback: " + name)
        return receipt


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--application", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--packet", action="append", required=True,
                        help="Decoded source JSON packet; repeat in explicit layer order")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    print(json.dumps(run(args.application, args.packet, dry_run=args.dry_run),
                     indent=2, sort_keys=True))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Exact, scalable one-dimensional precipitation subset matching.

The smaller target population is injected into distinct candidate cells, minimizing
sum(abs(target - candidate)). Sorting is O((n+m) log(n+m)); diagonal separation is
O(n log(m-n+1)) time and O(n+m) storage, without a pairwise matrix. See the adjacent
MATCHED_CONTROL_MATCHING.md for the scientific contract and tie convention.

Algorithm: Aggarwal, Bar-Noy, Khuller, Kravets and Schieber, CS-TR-3199,
section 4 (bitonic Monge arrays). This is an original NumPy implementation.
https://hdl.handle.net/1903/610
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
import math
from typing import Callable, Any

import numpy as np

METHOD = "class-stratified-exact-monge-L1-dyadic/v1"
TIE_RULE = "sorted-value-id; symbolic target=3*i+1, candidate=3*j; first prefix minimum"
_CHUNK = 262_144  # Temporary-array size only; every input cell is processed.
_INT_LIMIT = 1 << 61


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Matching:
    """Positions refer to the caller's original arrays, not sorted ordinals."""
    candidate_positions: np.ndarray
    target_order: np.ndarray
    target_count: int
    candidate_count: int
    objective_integer: int
    objective_binary_exponent: int
    arithmetic: str
    separator_rows: int
    separators: int

    def metadata(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        try:
            objective = math.ldexp(float(self.objective_integer), self.objective_binary_exponent)
            if not math.isfinite(objective):
                objective = None
        except OverflowError:
            objective = None
        return {
            "method": METHOD, "tie_rule": TIE_RULE,
            "target_cells": self.target_count, "eligible_candidate_cells": self.candidate_count,
            "objective_sum_absolute_precipitation_residual_mm_year": objective,
            "exact_objective": {"integer": str(self.objective_integer),
                                "binary_exponent": self.objective_binary_exponent},
            "arithmetic": self.arithmetic, "separator_rows": self.separator_rows,
            "separators": self.separators,
            "optimization": "global minimum total absolute precipitation residual",
            "matching_scope": "one already-selected original land-cover class",
        }


def _check(callback: Callable[[], None] | None) -> None:
    if callback is not None:
        callback()  # Exceptions propagate; the caller owns its checkpoint/queue.


def _values(value: Any, label: str) -> np.ndarray:
    arr = np.asarray(value)
    if arr.ndim != 1 or arr.dtype.kind not in "fiu":
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a one-dimensional real numeric array")
    if arr.dtype.kind == "f" and arr.dtype.itemsize > 8:
        raise ValueError(f"{label}: explicitly choose float64 before matching higher-precision inputs")
    if arr.dtype.kind in "iu" and arr.size and (
            int(arr.min()) < -(1 << 53) or int(arr.max()) > (1 << 53)):
        raise ValueError(f"{label}: integer coordinates must be exactly representable in float64")
    arr = np.asarray(arr, dtype=np.float64)
    if not np.isfinite(arr).all():
        raise ValueError(f"{label} contains nonfinite precipitation; resolve source support first")
    if np.any(arr < 0):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} contains negative precipitation")
    return arr


def _ids(value: Any, count: int, label: str) -> np.ndarray:
    if value is None:
        return np.arange(count, dtype=np.int64)
    arr = np.asarray(value)
    if arr.ndim != 1 or arr.size != count or arr.dtype.kind not in "iu":
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must contain one integer original cell ID per value")
    if arr.size and (int(arr.min()) < 0 or int(arr.max()) > np.iinfo(np.int64).max):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be nonnegative signed-64-bit cell IDs")
    arr = np.asarray(arr, dtype=np.int64)
    if count > 1 and not np.all(arr[1:] > arr[:-1]) and np.unique(arr).size != count:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} contains duplicate original cell IDs")
    return arr


def _binary_unit(arrays: tuple[np.ndarray, ...], callback: Callable[[], None] | None) -> int:
    """Smallest binary unit represented by the actual IEEE-754 input values."""
    unit = None
    for array in arrays:
        for start in range(0, array.size, _CHUNK):
            _check(callback)
            bits = array[start:start + _CHUNK].view(np.uint64)
            exponent = ((bits >> np.uint64(52)) & np.uint64(2047)).astype(np.int64)
            significand = bits & np.uint64((1 << 52) - 1)
            significand = significand | ((exponent != 0).astype(np.uint64) << np.uint64(52))
            nonzero = significand != 0
            if not np.any(nonzero):
                continue
            sig = significand[nonzero]
            # The isolated low bit is a power of two and converts to float exactly.
            low = sig & (~sig + np.uint64(1))
            trailing = np.frexp(low.astype(np.float64))[1].astype(np.int64) - 1
            e = exponent[nonzero]
            powers = np.where(e == 0, -1074, e - 1075) + trailing
            local = int(powers.min())
            unit = local if unit is None else min(unit, local)
    return 0 if unit is None else unit


def _coordinates(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray, callback: Callable[[], None] | None
                 ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, int, str]:
    unit = _binary_unit((a, b), callback)
    maximum = max(float(a.max(initial=0)), float(b.max(initial=0)))
    try:
        scaled_maximum = math.ldexp(maximum, -unit)
    except OverflowError:
        scaled_maximum = math.inf
    # Nonnegative coordinates <=2**61 guarantee safe signed differences. Prefix
    # absolute differences are bounded by the telescoping candidate value range.
    fast = scaled_maximum <= _INT_LIMIT
    converted = []
    for arr in (a, b):
        out = np.empty(arr.size, dtype=np.int64 if fast else object)
        for start in range(0, arr.size, _CHUNK):
            _check(callback)
            stop = min(arr.size, start + _CHUNK)
            if fast:
                scaled = np.ldexp(arr[start:stop], -unit)
                out[start:stop] = scaled.astype(np.int64)
            else:
                for j in range(start, stop):
                    numerator, denominator = float(arr[j]).as_integer_ratio()
                    shift = -(denominator.bit_length() - 1) - unit
                    out[j] = numerator << shift if shift >= 0 else numerator >> (-shift)
        converted.append(out)
    return converted[0], converted[1], unit, "int64-dyadic" if fast else "python-integer-dyadic"


def _exact_sum(arr: np.ndarray) -> int:
    total = 0
    for start in range(0, arr.size, _CHUNK):
        part = arr[start:start + _CHUNK]
        if part.dtype == object or (part.size and int(part.max()) * part.size > np.iinfo(np.int64).max):
            total += sum(map(int, part))
        else:
            total += int(part.sum(dtype=np.int64))
    return total


def match_precipitation(target_values: Any, candidate_values: Any, *,
                        target_ids: Any = None, candidate_ids: Any = None,
                        check_running: Callable[[], None] | None = None) -> Matching:
    """Match all targets to distinct candidates with the exact minimum L1 cost.

    Input values are finite, nonnegative float64 precipitation in mm/year. IDs
    are unique nonnegative original cell indices within each population. This
    primitive does not choose geographic/corridor/class support: its caller must
    supply that support and must enforce disjoint target/candidate populations.
    Empty target classes are valid. Insufficient candidates raise ValueError.

    No user input is rounded, binned or perturbed. Symbolic secondary coordinates
    only choose among exactly equal primary objectives. Legacy DP tie-selected
    cell identities may differ: retain existing completed editions unchanged.
    """
    _check(check_running)
    targets = _values(target_values, "targets")
    candidates = _values(candidate_values, "candidates")
    n, m = targets.size, candidates.size
    if n > m:
        raise ValueError(f"Insufficient disjoint candidates: {m} available for {n} targets")
    ti = _ids(target_ids, n, "target_ids")
    ci = _ids(candidate_ids, m, "candidate_ids")
    if not n:
        empty = np.empty(0, dtype=np.int64)
        return Matching(empty, empty, 0, m, 0, 0, "int64-dyadic", 0, 0)
    # Secondary prefix arithmetic is also exact. This bound is far beyond grids
    # that fit in addressable arrays, but reject rather than allow int64 overflow.
    if 12 * n * (m + n + 1) >= np.iinfo(np.int64).max:
        raise OverflowError("Symbolic tie-coordinate population exceeds signed-64-bit accumulation")
    _check(check_running)
    to = np.lexsort((ti, targets))
    co = np.lexsort((ci, candidates))
    a, b, exponent, arithmetic = _coordinates(targets[to], candidates[co], check_running)
    selected = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    # Process the disjoint recursion nodes a level at a time. Every level is
    # vectorized; there is no Python loop per target cell or candidate pair.
    starts = np.array([0], dtype=np.int64)
    stops = np.array([n], dtype=np.int64)
    lefts = np.array([0], dtype=np.int64)
    rights = np.array([m - n], dtype=np.int64)
    rows_visited = separators = 0
    while starts.size:
        _check(check_running)
        lengths = stops - starts
        group_starts = np.concatenate((np.array([0], dtype=np.int64), np.cumsum(lengths[:-1])))
        rows = np.arange(int(lengths.sum()), dtype=np.int64) + np.repeat(starts - group_starts, lengths)
        fixed = lefts == rights
        if np.any(fixed):
            fixed_rows = np.repeat(fixed, lengths)
            selected[rows[fixed_rows]] = rows[fixed_rows] + np.repeat(lefts, lengths)[fixed_rows]
            if np.all(fixed):
                break
            starts, stops, lefts, rights = (v[~fixed] for v in (starts, stops, lefts, rights))
            lengths = stops - starts
            group_starts = np.concatenate((np.array([0], dtype=np.int64), np.cumsum(lengths[:-1])))
            rows = np.arange(int(lengths.sum()), dtype=np.int64) + np.repeat(starts - group_starts, lengths)
        middle = (lefts + rights) // 2
        offsets = np.repeat(middle, lengths)
        j = rows + offsets
        rows_visited += int(rows.size)
        separators += int(starts.size)
        x, lo, hi = a[rows], b[j], b[j + 1]
        # A full diagonal is cost(i, i+offset). The prefix minimizer of adjacent
        # diagonal differences is the separating row (CS-TR-3199, section 4.2).
        prefix = np.cumsum(np.abs(x - lo) - np.abs(x - hi))
        before = np.concatenate((np.array([0], dtype=prefix.dtype), prefix[group_starts[1:] - 1]))
        primary = prefix - np.repeat(before, lengths)
        # The scanned candidate gaps are disjoint and ascending even across
        # groups. Their total bounds every primary prefix by b[-1]-b[0], so
        # int64 accumulation cannot overflow under _coordinates' range bound.
        # Distinct symbolic coordinates resolve repeated-value plateaus without
        # rounding/perturbing any actual precipitation: target (value,3*i+1),
        # candidate (value,3*j). Secondary diagonal costs depend only on offset.
        d_lo = 1 - 3 * offsets
        d_hi = d_lo - 3
        secondary_lo = np.where(x == lo, np.abs(d_lo), np.where(x > lo, d_lo, -d_lo))

    positions[to] = co[selected]
    return Matching(positions, to, n, m, objective, exponent, arithmetic, rows_visited, separators)
